Final Project and Final Assessment (Part 3: Sessions 25 and 26)

The course's capstone, closing Part 3 and the whole course. The final project is Lesson 10.1's: each learner chooses one of seven client briefs (or their own idea within the size rules), plans it on the kit's worksheet, builds it from the kit's starter in about 30 more hours (usually 25 to 35) over four to six weeks, launches it without a paid account (an internal preview build or a recording on a real phone), has it reviewed by a peer and shows it in Session 26. The source is the final-project kit (downloads/final-project-kit/: README, worksheet, seven briefs, rubric, peer review, starter). This section adds only the instructor's side: the timeline, milestone check-ins, scoring notes for each rubric row, the Session 26 run-sheet, a scoring sheet, how results are recorded, and the course's written final assessment (24 items on all three parts, with its key). The rubric below is the kit's rubric.md, unchanged.

  • The kit and the size rules · the timeline from Session 25 to the final scores · milestone check-ins
  • The rubric (Lesson 10.1, verbatim) · scoring notes per row · scoring habits · the scoring sheet · recording results

starter/An Expo SDK 58 project with the course's conventions and none of Shoreline Crew: one example Item, an in-app mock API (EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL=demo) the tests share through MSW, 22 tests, three variants, eas.json, CIMilestone 1 (types next to Item), Milestone 2 (deletes it)

Size rules for an own idea (briefs.md): three to six must-haves, five to ten screens, at most two kinds of people, two device features used for a real reason, an offline plan, no paid service; health, money and children's data shrunk until they are not needed, or treated as the hardest part of the project. Written up in the briefs' shape before the project starts, so the reviewer can hold the author to it.

If Session 26 must follow Session 25 within a week

The project cannot be finished in a week (Lesson 10.1: about 30 more hours, usually 25 to 35, over four to six weeks). Run Session 26 as a progress showcase (Milestones 1 to 3, the same five-minute format with "what's next" stretched) and the written final assessment as planned, then set a final evidence date four to six weeks later and score the rubric from that evidence. Say so in Session 25.

The rubric (Lesson 10.1's rubric.md, verbatim)

Nothing in this rubric needs money. No row needs an Apple Developer Program membership, a Google Play account, a paid Expo plan or a paid server. Where a row mentions store accounts, it is one way to reach "strong", never the only one.

#Criterion (modules)Not yet (0)Meets (1)Strong (2)
1Plan (10; every module's "your own app" notes)Worksheet sections missing, or copied from Shoreline Crew without thoughtEvery section filled for this brief; decisions have reasons; milestones and time log keptTrade-offs argued with evidence (local vs server data, Expo Go vs development build, what is out of scope and why); estimate vs actual hours reflected on
2Screens and navigation (2, 4)A screen that is blank, cut off or unreachable; a dead end with no way back; text under the notch or the home indicatorEvery screen in the worksheet's route plan works; safe areas respected; light and dark both readable; a not-found screen; at least one screen opens from a deep linkTabs, stacks and modals chosen per the worksheet's reasons; a wide screen (tablet, a phone on its side, the web preview) uses the space; linked screens have something sensible underneath
3Data and server state (1.3, 3, 5.1, 5.2)any or as to silence errors; API data used before it is checked; server data copied into useState; lists that do not update after a changeDomain types in types.ts with unions and complete Record tables; every answer checked; TanStack Query factories and mutations that invalidate the right keys; loading, error (Try again), empty and not-found states in words people understand; npx tsc --noEmit cleanComputed values never stored; long lists measured and fast (FlashList or paging where the worksheet planned it); refetch on returning to the app and on reconnecting works on a phone
4Storage and offline (5.3, 5.5)A token or secret in AsyncStorage or in the code; data lost on a restart that the plan said to keep; the app breaks or spins forever without a connectionEvery piece of kept data in the store the worksheet chose (SecureStore for secrets only); what the app does offline is written down and works: a queue with ids made on the phone, or a clear "you are offline" with the last answer, or local-only dataOffline changes tested (a resend creates no duplicate); the person can see what has not been sent yet; sign-out clears what it should
5Forms and input (2.4, 5.4)Fields without labels; errors only in the console; the keyboard covers the field being typed inOne schema per form for its rules and types; the right keyboard, return keys that move to the next field; errors under their fields, the server's own rules included; nothing hidden by the keyboardThumb controls where they beat typing (steppers, choices, switches); the form survives a slow or failed send without losing what was typed

Plus a README with how to run it, and a peer review given and received, every point answeredTwo testers used it on their own phones and you acted on what they said; or (only if you already have the accounts) a build on Google Play internal testing or TestFlight; a written reflection on what you would do differently

Total ____ / 20. Rows at "not yet": ____. The project is complete when no row is "not yet"; "not yet" is not a failing grade, it is the list of what to do next; "strong" rows are what make it a portfolio piece.

Scoring notes for instructors

For each row: where the evidence is, how to check "meets" quickly, and how to tell "meets" from "strong" when it is close. These notes never change what a row asks for; when they seem to, the rubric wins. No phone was used to write them: what a row asks to see on a phone, you see on the learner's phone, in their recording or on your own phone with their preview build.

RowEvidenceHow to check (meets)Meets or strong?

Planworksheet.md in the repository: the charter (section 0), sections 2 to 15, the milestones and time log (section 16); docs/decisions/ (Lesson 10.2).Every section names this brief's things, not Shoreline Crew's; decisions have reasons; the time log has actual hours, not only estimates. The evidence check's row 1 lines are the quick test.Strong needs a trade-off argued with evidence (local or server data, Expo Go or a development build, what is out of scope and why) and a sentence comparing estimated and actual hours.

Scoring habits
  • Score from evidence you opened, not from the demo's polish: a smooth five minutes can hide a red CI run, and a nervous demo can hide excellent work.
  • Self, peer and instructor scores differ by 2 on a row? Talk before you record it; usually one of you missed a piece of evidence.
  • A row is "not yet" only when its "meets" column is not met. Write the one sentence that would move it to "meets" next to the 0.
  • The scope is the learner's: do not score down a must-have the charter put out of scope with a reason. "Not possible yet: no https server" on the release checklist is an honest pass (row 9).
  • One platform is fine: "checked on Android only" (or iPhone only) is an honest line in worksheet section 1. Never ask for a paid account, a store listing or a Mac.
  • The evidence check (labs/module-26/showcase-preflight/evidence_check.mjs) reads files only; it is a list of missing evidence, never a score. As downloaded, the kit's starter gets 9 FIX lines (the starter's names, ids, slug and scheme, the app config test, no worksheet, the example Item, only the starter's tests, the starter's README): a project that still shows them is not ready to be scored.

Question bank
  • Which value do you compute instead of storing, and why?
  • What does the app do with no signal, and how do you know nothing is sent twice?
  • Which rule does only your mock API keep, and where is its test?
  • What happens when someone answers "Don't allow"?
  • What did you put out of scope, and what would it take to add it?
  • Where were your estimates furthest from the actual hours, and why?
  • What did your peer review find that you had missed?
Class sizeFormat
Up to 12Two rounds of six 7-minute slots, as above
13 to 18Three rounds of 5-minute slots (4 demo, 1 question; the rest on cards); the evidence results read out in 2 minutes
19 or moreA gallery: half the room presents at stations for 25 minutes while the other half visits, then swap; you visit every station for a 4-minute demo. Or a second showcase block before Session 26
If…Then
The venue network blocks phones from the laptopThe preview build needs no laptop and demo data needs no server; otherwise the learner's recording
A learner has no launch yetDemo in Expo Go or the web preview from the laptop; row 10 is "not yet" with a plan, nothing else changes
A learner is absentA recorded five-minute demo sent by the evidence date counts as the showcase
A demo overrunsThe timekeeper stands at 5:00 and 7:00; the rest goes on cards

Recording results

  • Final project: complete when no rubric row is at 0 (the rubric's own definition), by the end of the resubmission window; record the total out of 20 and the rows at "strong" for references and portfolio notes.
  • Written final assessment: 27 points (21 multiple-choice items at 1 point, 3 short answers at 2 points). Pass mark: 19 (19 of 27, 70 %). Below it: go through the wrong items with the learner and offer a parallel retake of your choice (the same lessons, other items).
  • Course complete = final project complete AND the written final assessment passed: the final project complete under Lesson 10.1's rubric, and at least 19 of 27 points on the written final. The Part 1 and Part 2 results (above) are the results when a part runs on its own.
  • Late work: the resubmission window is the late window. After it, "not yet" rows stay "not yet" and the learner gets a written list of what would complete them.

Written final assessment: learner pages

Instructions (read aloud)

Closed book, no laptops, 35 minutes. 24 items on the whole course: Part 1 (F1 to F8), Part 2 (F9 to F16), Part 3 (F17 to F24). Multiple choice: circle one letter (1 point). Short answer: one or two sentences (2 points). Every output shown is real: the course lessons' own outputs (the ones marked "on a phone" are quoted, as the lessons quote them, from the library's own code) and a run of the final-project starter. Total 27 points; pass mark: 19 (19 of 27, 70 %). Name: ____________________

Changing numColumns on the fly is not supported. Change the key prop on FlatList when changing the number of columns to force a fresh render of the component.
A) Never use numColumns

C) Use a ScrollView with map

A) Its own ScrollView
B) An index as its key

Why: Virtualized lists render a window of rows and recycle the rest; a stable key from the id lets them keep the right state on the right row when the data changes. Lesson 3.2.
